source: Order adapted from the Daily Turkish deck: each lemma of its ranked list (itself adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, CC BY-SA 4.0, built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus) was matched by meaning to its usual Turkmen equivalent, then edited by hand: film-dialogue words dropped or moved down, Turkish lemmas that share one Turkmen word merged, everyday Turkmen words added where their use would put them. Ranks are an editorial estimate, not a Turkmen corpus count. The ranked list is scripts/turkmen/tm-wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkmen/TM-PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

ex.en: Merjen doesn't go to work on Tuesday.
We have no lessons on Wednesday.
My dad is going to Mary on Thursday.
There's a wedding in the village on Friday.
So why didn't he come, then?

cards.note: Bookish: it opens a question, often one the speaker asks themself.

ex.en: We rest on Saturday.
I don't go anywhere on Sunday.
There are many tall buildings in Ashgabat.
This time suits me.
There are a hundred tenge in a manat.
The Nowruz holiday is in March.
Aýna spread the cloth for the guests' meal.
Show me your passport, please.
The old man wears a telpek in winter.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *telpegi*.

ex.en: My suitcase is very heavy.
All the relatives came to the wedding.

en: a mark of respect (after a woman's name)

ex.en: My aunt lives in Dashoguz.

cards.note: Your mother's sister; your father's sister is *bibi*. After a woman's name it shows respect: *Jeren daýza*.

ex.en: The sun sets in the west.
My aunt came to visit us.

cards.note: Your father's sister; your mother's sister is *daýza*.

ex.en: The sun rises in the east.
The weather was terrible yesterday.
The children are running in the park.
The plane leaves Ashgabat at five.
We live in the twenty-first century.
My father works in an office.
There are four seasons in a year.
Bye, see you tomorrow!

cards.note: Said by the one leaving; to several people, or politely, *hoş galyň*. The one who stays says *ak ýol*.

ex.en: Her hair is long and black.
There are lots of shops on this street.
There's no internet at home.
I was born in Turkmenabat.

cards.note: Its second vowel drops before a vowel: *doglan* (born), *doglup*.

ex.tk: Ol her aý täze žurnal satyn alýar.
ex.en: She buys a new magazine every month.
My grandfather has four grandchildren.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *agtygy*.

ex.en: This is impossible.
The roof of the house is red.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *üçegi*.

ex.en: The bride wore a beautiful red robe.
We have enough time.
There are three tea bowls on the table.
The lift isn't working, take the stairs.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *basgançagy*.

ex.en: The milk is in the fridge.
Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan.
In winter we light the stove at home.
What animals are there in your village?
There are lots of stars in the desert at night.
There's a new bridge over the river.
Good morning, teacher!

cards.note: To one person you call *sen*: *Ertiriň haýyrly bolsun*.

ex.en: This room is shared by everyone.
There's a big square in the town centre.
Our district is near Mary.

cards.note: p becomes b before a vowel: *etraby*.

ex.en: This is an ancient fortress.
The school's rules are strict.
The old minaret stands in the middle of the town.
This is bad news.
There's an old well in the village.
Where's the bus stop?
The farmers take water from the canal.
I drink coffee in the morning.
In autumn the leaves turn yellow.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *ýapragy*.

ex.en: The pharmacy is open at night too.
I grew up in a village.
We had dinner at a restaurant.
There are old carpets in the museum.
The result isn't known yet.
Let's go to the theatre on Saturday!
This chair is very comfortable.

cards.note: ç becomes j before a vowel: *oturgyjy*.

ex.tk: Men hat ibermek üçin poçta gitdim.
ex.en: I went to the post office to send a letter.
Scholars are studying old carpets.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *derňär*, *derňäp*.

ex.en: The airport isn't far from the town.
Open your notebooks.
The railway runs through the desert.

ex.tk: Bu sözlemi iňlis diline terjime et.
ex.en: Translate this sentence into English.

cards.note: *etmek* changes t to d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *terjime edýär*, *terjime eder*.

ex.en: A giraffe's neck is very long.

cards.note: Its second vowel drops before a vowel: *boýny*, *boýnum* (my neck).

ex.en: Be careful on the road!
My shoulders ache.
Do you have a pen?
My knee hurts after football.
The baby cried in the night.
Her lips are red.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *dodagy*.

ex.en: Turn on the lamp, the room is dark.
Our son-in-law works as a doctor.
Take a breath, don't worry.
My nephew started school this year.
The baby's fingers are tiny.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *barmagy*. Not the verb *barmak* (to go).

ex.en: The nurse gave me some medicine.

cards.note: Literally sister of mercy: only *uýa* takes the endings, so *şepagat uýalary* (nurses).

ex.en: I can't stand the cold.
My brother works as an engineer.
The whole nation knows this song.
She's a famous singer.
I miss my home.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *küýsär*, *küýsäp*.

ex.en: The painter painted a picture of the mountain.
I've lost my key.
The police came at once.
How much is this shirt?

en: to be busy with, to take up

ex.en: I do sport.
I got you a present for your birthday.

cards.note: t becomes d before a vowel: *sowgady*, *sowgadym* (my present).

ex.en: The teenagers are playing football.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *ýetginjegi*.

ex.en: There are twenty pupils in our class.
A farmer's work is hard.
Give me a bowl of tea, please.
There's hot tea in the teapot.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *çäýnegi*.

ex.en: His salary is good.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *aýlygy*.

ex.en: This mattress is soft.
This table is a bit low.
At home, do exercise three in writing.
The children are playing ball in the street.
Last night I had a strange dream.
Look this word up in the dictionary.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *sözlügi*.

ex.en: At night the village is quiet.
There are thirty letters in the Turkmen alphabet.
This street is very wide.
The children are learning the alphabet.
He'll come soon.
This shirt is tight on me.
Read this sentence out loud.
The room is bright and spacious.
Business is going well at the market.
I got home late.

cards.note: Not the noun *barmak* (finger).

ex.en: The melons at the market are very tasty.
What's new?

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *täzeligi*.

ex.tk: Bu dermany günde üç gezek içiň.
ex.en: Take this medicine three times a day.
Thank you, I'm full.
He's a good person.

cards.note: A little more literary than *gowy*; common in proverbs and wishes.

ex.en: There's water in my bag.
Our teacher is very kind.
Birds fly south in autumn.
In summer we swim in the sea.
The air is humid by the sea.
The driver drives the bus slowly.
Türkmenbaşy is on the shore of the Caspian Sea.

cards.note: Its second vowel drops before a vowel: *deňzi*, *Hazar deňzi* (the Caspian Sea).

ex.en: The seller gave us cheap grapes.
We bought the things we need for the trip.
Swimming is good for the body.
My father is a good cook.
Life in the city is expensive.
The farmers are picking cotton.
The shepherd's dog is a big Alabay.
I water the flowers every evening.
The mechanic fixed my car.
The children are picking apples in the orchard.
The new study programme is ready.
I go to work by bike.
Dad cut the watermelon into four pieces.
This box is empty.
The doctor measured my height.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *ölçär*, *ölçäp*.

ex.tk: Ol çagalar üçin täze oýun döretdi.
ex.en: He created a new game for children.

cards.note: t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *döredýär*, *döredip*; it stays before a consonant: *döretdi*.

ex.en: Happy birthday!
Nature in the mountains is very beautiful.
We painted the wall white.
Turkmen culture is ancient and rich.
We decorated the house for New Year.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *bezär*, *bezäp*.

ex.en: Every nation has its own traditions.
Grandpa has got old, but he still works.

ex.tk: Bu meniň syrym, hiç kime aýtma.
ex.en: This is my secret, don't tell anyone.
Dad is fishing in the river.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *balygy*.

ex.en: The door suddenly opened.

en: to fill up, to become full

ex.en: The bus filled up with people.
There's a big park near our house.
Take this letter to the director.
The hero defeated the enemy.
The host offered us tea.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-r* and *-p*: *hödürlär*, *hödürläp*.

ex.en: Tie your horse to the tree.
The teacher praised me.
I wrote a list for the market.

en: to put up, to set upright

ex.en: We planted trees in front of the school.
I wrote a letter to my friend.
A lot of snow fell this year.

cards.note: Colloquial for *köp*. *Kän sag bol!* (thanks a lot).

ex.en: Everyone wants peace.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *parahatçylygy*.

ex.en: It's a bit cold today.
Mountain air is clean.
There's an English exam tomorrow.

ex.tk: Haçan-da men öýe gelenimde, ol ýatypdy.
ex.en: When I came home, he had gone to bed.

cards.note: Written and formal; in speech the verb in *-An* alone is enough: *Men öýe gelenimde*.

ex.en: Our brain rests while we sleep.
She talked about her family.
The tea is hot, be careful.

ex.tk: Bu ýerde hiç hili howp ýok.
ex.en: There's no danger here.
The school is near our house.
Friendship is worth more than money.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *dostlugy*.

ex.en: We stayed at home because of the rain.
Which sport do you like?
Hi, Merdan! How are you?

cards.note: To someone you call *siz*: *Ýagdaýlaryňyz nähili?*

ex.en: If only you'd come too!
There's a beautiful lake in the mountains.
My name is Aýna. Pleased to meet you!
Walking in the desert at night is dangerous.
We stayed at the hotel for three days.
Good night, see you tomorrow.

cards.note: To one person you call *sen*: *Gijäň rahat bolsun*.

ex.tk: Men bu aý köp pul harçladym.
ex.en: I spent a lot of money this month.

ex.tk: Ak ýol! Ýetenden soň jaň et.
ex.en: Have a good trip! Call when you get there.

cards.note: Said to the one leaving; the one leaving says *hoş gal*.

ex.en: There's a lot of sand in the Garagum.
This carpet's göls are red.
In winter it gets dark early.
In the village they keep sheep and goats.
This question is very simple.
This is a good opportunity, use it.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *mümkinçiligi*.

ex.en: She lives in a small town by the sea.
Her level of Turkmen is high.
This film is very interesting.
We cooked chicken for dinner.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *towugy*.

ex.en: Hot soup is good in winter.
I drink my tea with honey in it.

cards.note: Also a point or mark: *bäş bal* (five points).
